source.label: Second moment of the complete-grid Gram form with several off-line pairs

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: For every finite conjugation-closed configuration Z in the complete-grid Gram model with real even window phi supported in [-Lam/2,Lam/2]: ||G_Z||_HS^2 = ||phi||_2^-4 int_{-Lam}^{Lam} (phi^2*phi^2)(s) |S_Z(s)|^2 ds, S_Z(s) = sum_z m_z e^{-isz} = sum_real m e^{-is gamma} + 2 sum_j m_j e^{-is gamma_j} cosh(delta_j s).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof from the bilinear Gram identity and conjugation invariance. Identifies the Hilbert-Schmidt norm at bandwidth Lam with a weighted mean square of the zero sum over |log x| <= Lam. Abstract statement about configurations; no estimate for zeta zeros.
claims.rationale: Makes explicit that a second-moment premise at bandwidth Lam is a mean-square bound for the exponential sum over the points; expected to be the classical mean-square form of pair-correlation sums, novelty not claimed.
claims.next_action: Use for the cluster question: lower bounds for the mean square with positive integer coefficients.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry; trapezoid-rule control against grid sums on 22 configurations agrees to the stated tolerance.
notes.significance: Context-level identity; novelty not claimed and not searched in the literature.
notes.relationships: Depends on the pair atom spectrum's bilinear Gram identity.

claims.summary: Flat window, complete grid, all points real, at most M_loc points (with multiplicity) per cell of length 2 pi/Lam over K consecutive cells: lambda_max(G_Z) <= M_loc (3 + (2/pi)(1 + ln K)); for every window ||G_Z||_HS^2 <= lambda_max(G_Z) * (number of points with multiplicity).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: Gram matrix of unit vectors, absolute row sums, the sinc decay. Shows that in the model a configuration of real points with a local count satisfies a second-moment bound at every bandwidth, so that bound is a consequence of the statement to be proved rather than an independent input.
claims.rationale: Answers whether the second-moment premise beyond bandwidth log T follows from all points being real; it does, in the flat-window model, given a local count.
claims.next_action: None beyond use in the many-pair bound; a smooth-window version is not needed at present.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof in the entry for the flat window; control on 18 configurations with real points tests the direction only.
notes.relationships: Uses the trace statement of solitary amplification; used in the many-pair norm bound's reduction.

claims.summary: Complete-grid Gram model with n off-axis pairs, G = P + B: ||G||_HS >= ||B||_HS - ||P||_HS and lambda_max(G) >= ||B||_HS/(2n)^(3/2); ||B||_HS^2 >= 2 rho sum m_j^2 kappa_j^2 - sum m_j m_l (1 + kappa(delta_j - delta_l)) with rho the least eigenvalue of the normalized Gram matrix of the exponentials e^{-is z_j} in L^2(phi^2*phi^2); flat window with delta_j Lam >= 1, delta_j <= Delta and heights 8 Delta-separated: rho >= 3/5, and ||B||_HS >= kappa_max when kappa_max >= 5 M^2 + 1.
claims.assessment: Working proof. Extends solitary amplification to any number of off-line pairs with the loss stated exactly as rho; no loss in b for height-separated pairs. For clusters rho can be tiny and the bound empty, while sampled clusters show the true norm is not small, so the cluster case is open rather than obstructed. Conditional on an unavailable second-moment premise beyond bandwidth log T for any consequence about zeros.
claims.rationale: Shows what a second-moment bound at large bandwidth would exclude (separated off-line pairs) and what it leaves (clusters); with the real configuration bound, shows the premise is close to a restatement of the goal for separated exceptions.
claims.next_action: Bound the mean square for clusters with positive integer multiplicities, or find a cluster of simple points with a loss beyond every power of b.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof of all five parts in the entry; part 5 for the flat window only. Numerical control on 22 configurations.
notes.significance: Context: delimits the Gram route in the model; not a result about zeta. Novelty not claimed.
notes.relationships: Refines solitary amplification (n = 1 gives a solitary-type bound up to constants); depends on the pair atom spectrum, the second-moment identity's Gram interpretation and the real configuration bound; consistent with the two-pair cancellation.

relationships: Uses both Gram identities and kappa.
Uses its trace statement in the eigenvalue argument.
